title: The simple future: hablaré
summary: Predict, promise and guess: hablaré, tendrás, hará, podremos, saldréis, vendrán.
focus: Futuro simple: infinitive + é, ás, á, emos, éis, án, and the irregular stems
content:
## One set of endings on the infinitive

The **futuro simple** is the easiest tense to build. Keep the **whole infinitive** and add six endings. They are the same for **-ar**, **-er** and **-ir** verbs.

| person | ending | hablar | comer | vivir |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| yo | **-é** | hablar**é** | comer**é** | vivir**é** |
| tú | **-ás** | hablar**ás** | comer**ás** | vivir**ás** |
| él / ella / usted | **-á** | hablar**á** | comer**á** | vivir**á** |
| nosotros/as | **-emos** | hablar**emos** | comer**emos** | vivir**emos** |
| vosotros/as | **-éis** | hablar**éis** | comer**éis** | vivir**éis** |
| ellos / ellas / ustedes | **-án** | hablar**án** | comer**án** | vivir**án** |

Every form has a written accent except **nosotros**: *hablaremos*, not *hablarémos*.

- *Mañana hablaré con el jefe.* (Tomorrow I will talk to the boss.)
- *Algún día viviremos en Madrid.* (One day we will live in Madrid.)

## Twelve irregular stems

Some verbs shorten the infinitive before taking the **same endings**. There are three patterns.

| pattern | verbs |
|---|---|
| drop the **e** | poder → **podr**é, saber → **sabr**é, querer → **querr**é, caber → **cabr**é, haber → **habr**á (there will be) |
| swap the vowel for **d** | tener → **tendr**é, poner → **pondr**é, salir → **saldr**é, venir → **vendr**é, valer → **valdr**é |
| shortened | hacer → **har**é, decir → **dir**é |

- *No podré venir el sábado.* (I won't be able to come on Saturday.)
- *¿Qué haremos esta noche?* (What will we do tonight?)
- *Te diré la verdad.* (I will tell you the truth.)

Compounds copy their parent: *mantener → mantendré*, *deshacer → desharé*.

## What the future is for

- **Predictions** about what will happen: *Mañana lloverá en el norte.* (Tomorrow it will rain in the north.) *Seguro que aprobarás el examen.* (I'm sure you'll pass the exam.)
- **Promises** and firm commitments: *Te llamaré esta noche, lo prometo.* (I'll call you tonight, I promise.)
- **Guessing about the present** (probability). This use has no English *will*: *¿Qué hora es?* (What time is it?) *Serán las tres.* (It must be about three.) *¿Dónde está Juan?* (Where is Juan?) *Estará en casa.* (He's probably at home.)

Time markers: *mañana*, *pasado mañana*, *el año que viene*, *el mes que viene*, *dentro de dos días* (two days from now), *algún día*.

## Ir a + infinitive or the future?

You already know **ir a + infinitive** (*voy a comer*). Both talk about later, but they sound different.

| | ir a + infinitive | futuro simple |
|---|---|---|
| plans already decided | *Esta noche vamos a cenar fuera.* | |
| the very near future | *Va a llover, mira el cielo.* | |
| predictions, promises | | *El año que viene tendré un coche nuevo.* *Te llamaré.* |
| guessing about now | | *Serán las tres.* |

In everyday speech **ir a** is much more common for plans. The simple future sounds more formal or more distant. Mixing them up is rarely a serious mistake, but the probability use (*serán las tres*) only works with the simple future.

vocabulary.example_meaning: My cousins will come in August.
Tomorrow I'll tell you the truth.

vocabulary.example: El año que viene viviré en Lisboa.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Next year I'll live in Lisbon.

vocabulary.example: El mes que viene cambiaré de trabajo.
Pasado mañana vamos a cenar fuera.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The day after tomorrow we're going out for dinner.

vocabulary.meaning: in (an amount of time from now)
vocabulary.example: Dentro de dos años tendré un coche nuevo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: In two years I'll have a new car.
One day we'll live in Madrid.
Tomorrow it will rain in the north.
I'm sure you'll pass the exam.
The exam will be on Monday.

quiz.prompt: Complete with the future of vivir: Algún día (nosotros) ___ en Madrid.
quiz.explanation: Keep the infinitive and add -emos: 'viviremos'. The nosotros form is the only one without an accent.
Weather verbs use the él/ella form: infinitive 'llover' + -á = 'lloverá'. The infinitive keeps its own vowel, so 'llovará' is wrong.
hints: 'It' rains, which is third person singular.

quiz.prompt: Complete with the future of tener: Dentro de dos años (yo) ___ un coche nuevo.
quiz.explanation: Tener has the irregular stem tendr-: 'tendré'. The endings never change.
hints: Tener swaps its vowel for a d.

quiz.prompt: Te lo prometo: te ___ esta noche.
quiz.explanation: A promise uses the simple future, and the speaker (yo) is promising: 'te llamaré'. 'Llamará' would mean someone else is calling.

quiz.prompt: Complete with the future of ser: ¿Qué hora es? — No sé, seguramente ___ las tres.
quiz.explanation: Guessing about the present uses the future: 'Serán las tres' means it must be about three. 'Las tres' is plural, so the verb takes the ellos form: serán.
hints: The future expresses probability about now.

quiz.prompt: Mis primos ___ a la boda el año que viene.
quiz.explanation: Venir has the irregular stem vendr- and ellos takes -án with an accent: 'vendrán'. 'Venderán' is from vender (to sell).
hints: Venir swaps its vowel for a d.

quiz.prompt: Complete with the future of decir: Mañana te ___ (yo) la verdad.
hints: Decir has a shortened stem, like hacer (har-).

quiz.explanation: A prediction: infinitive 'aprobar' + -ás = 'aprobarás'. Without the accent ('aprobaras') it is a different tense.

quiz.prompt: Choose the most natural way to say 'The day after tomorrow we're going to have dinner out' (a plan already decided).
options: Pasado mañana vamos a cenar fuera.
quiz.correct_answer: Pasado mañana vamos a cenar fuera.
quiz.explanation: A decided plan is most natural with ir a + infinitive, and the 'a' is required: 'vamos a cenar'. 'Cenábamos' is the past.
hints: Never drop the a in ir a + infinitive.

listening.meaning: This afternoon it will rain in Seville.
The day after tomorrow I'll go to the doctor.
listening.note: New word: el médico = the doctor.

listening.text: Mi hermana te dirá la verdad.
listening.meaning: My sister will tell you the truth.
listening.note: Decir shortens to dir- in the future.

listening.text: Seguramente aprobaréis el examen de inglés sin problemas.
listening.meaning: You'll probably pass the English exam without any problems.

listening.text: ¿Vendrás a mi casa el sábado por la tarde?
listening.meaning: Will you come to my house on Saturday afternoon?

listening.text: Te prometo que haré los deberes después de cenar.
listening.meaning: I promise I'll do my homework after dinner.
listening.note: New word: los deberes = the homework.

listening.text: Dentro de cinco años viviremos en una casa en la playa.
listening.meaning: In five years we'll live in a house on the beach.
listening.note: The nosotros form is the only one without an accent.

listening.text: El mes que viene mis padres vendrán a visitarnos a Madrid.
listening.meaning: Next month my parents will come to visit us in Madrid.

guide.tip: The future endings are the present of haber with an r in front. He, has, ha, hemos, habéis and han become -ré, -rás, -rá, -remos, -réis and -rán.

guide.section: Ir a + infinitive or the future

conversations.title: New Year's resolutions
conversations.scenario: It is just after midnight on New Year's Eve. Nuria and Pablo talk about the year ahead.

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: Happy New Year, Pablo! What will you do this year?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Seguramente cambiaré de trabajo. Y aprenderé a cocinar, te lo prometo.
lines.meaning: I'll probably change jobs. And I'll learn to cook, I promise.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¡Qué bien! Yo creo que viviré unos meses en Lisboa.
lines.meaning: Great! I think I'll live in Lisbon for a few months.

lines.speaker: b
lines.meaning: Really? And your boyfriend? Will he come with you?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: No lo sé. Él dice que no podrá dejar su trabajo.
lines.meaning: I don't know. He says he won't be able to leave his job.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Bueno, Lisboa está cerca. Tendréis tiempo para veros.
lines.meaning: Well, Lisbon is close. You'll have time to see each other.
lines.note: tener becomes tendr-, here in the vosotros form

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Sí. Y tú, ¿saldrás más? Siempre estás en casa.
lines.meaning: Yes. And you, will you go out more? You're always at home.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Este año saldré todos los sábados. Bueno, casi todos.
lines.meaning: This year I'll go out every Saturday. Well, almost every Saturday.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¿Qué hora es? ¿Y dónde están los demás?
lines.meaning: What time is it? And where are the others?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Serán las dos. Estarán bailando en el salón.
lines.meaning: It must be about two. They're probably dancing in the living room.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Pues vamos a bailar nosotros también.
lines.meaning: Then let's go and dance too.
lines.note: ir a + infinitive for a plan right now.

bites.title: Endings on the whole infinitive
bites.rule: Keep the infinitive and add -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis or -án. The same six endings work for -ar, -er and -ir verbs. Every form has an accent except nosotros.
bites.example_meaning: Tomorrow I will talk to the boss.

bites.title: Twelve irregular stems
bites.rule: The endings never change, only the stem: podr-, sabr-, querr-, cabr-, habr-, tendr-, pondr-, saldr-, vendr-, valdr-, har-, dir-.
bites.example: Tendré tiempo y haré la cena.
bites.example_meaning: I'll have time and I'll make dinner.

bites.title: Predict, promise, guess
bites.rule: Use the future for predictions (lloverá), promises (te llamaré) and guesses about right now (serán las tres means it must be three).
bites.example_meaning: Where is Juan? — He's probably at home.

bites.title: Decided plan? Use ir a
bites.rule: A plan you have already made sounds more natural with ir a + infinitive, as in vamos a cenar fuera. Keep the future for what you predict or promise.
bites.example: Esta noche vamos a cenar fuera.
bites.example_meaning: Tonight we're going to have dinner out.

sorts.title: Regular or irregular stem?
sorts.why: Tener becomes tendr-, hacer becomes har-, salir becomes saldr- and saber becomes sabr-. The rest keep the whole infinitive.

sorts.title: What is the speaker doing?
sorts.why: The same tense predicts the future, makes promises and guesses about the present (serán las tres means it must be three).

sorts.title: Who will do it?
sorts.why: -é marks yo, -ás marks tú, -á marks él/ella and -emos marks nosotros.

spots.sentence: Mañana yo hablaró con el jefe.
spots.why: Yo takes -é on the infinitive: hablaré.

spots.sentence: El año que viene teneré un coche.
spots.why: Tener has the irregular stem tendr-.
Hacer shortens to har- in the future.
The nosotros form is the only one without an accent.
Venir swaps its vowel for a d: vendr-.
Decir shortens to dir- in the future.
